heroHeadline: ICE Detention Hits Record 73,000 as Senate Enters $71.7B Reconciliation Floor Week; DHS Deportation Fleet Nearly Ready; ICE Director Blamed Deported Mother for Toddler's Killing; 3-Way Circuit Split on Mandatory Detention Heads Toward Supreme Court
heroSubtitle: As of May 17, 2026, ICE is holding a record 73,000 individuals in immigration detention — an 84% year-over-year increase — as the Senate begins the week of May 18 floor vote on the $71.7 billion ICE/CBP reconciliation package, now complicated by Senate Parliamentarian Byrd Rule rulings that struck key Border Patrol funding, DHS appropriations, and border security/technology provisions on May 14–15. A deep three-to-two circuit split on the Trump mandatory detention policy has now emerged after the 6th Circuit ruled it unconstitutional on May 11 (joining the 2nd and 11th Circuits), while the 5th and 8th Circuits upheld it — making Supreme Court review highly likely for a policy that could affect millions. On May 16, the Washington Post published an investigation finding that ICE acting director Todd Lyons publicly blamed Wendy Hernandez Reyes — a Honduran mother deported in January 2026 without her 2-year-old son Orlín — for 'abandoning' the child, who died in Florida in March showing signs of severe abuse; the Post found she had repeatedly begged ICE to reunite them. Also on May 16, CNN reported that DHS's new deportation fleet of 8 Boeing 737s and 2 Gulfstream jets is nearly operational, with a $70 million luxury 737 drawing Senate scrutiny. The 73,000-person detention population — held at a rate of one death every six days (30+ FY2026 deaths) — is maintained across 152 new facilities opened since January 2025, with 70.8% of detainees having no criminal conviction. Senate Republicans must rewrite Byrd Rule-struck provisions before the May 18 floor vote under Trump's June 1 signing deadline.
footerNote: Data sourced from DHS, ICE official records, ACLU, HRW, DHS OIG, TRAC Reports, Detention Watch Network, USCIS, ILRC, NIPNLG, Human Rights First, court records, Senate Budget Committee, and Congressional records
